problem:
$$
f(\theta ,ϕ)=⟨ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,ϕ\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\text{ _____ }⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(\theta ,ϕ)$ parametrizes the surface defined in spherical polar coordinates as

What is the third component of $f?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Parametrization of a Surface Defined in Spherical Polar Coordinates
examples.problem:
$$
\mathbf{f}(\theta,\phi) = \big\langle \text{_____}, \: \theta \sin\theta \sin^2 \phi, \: \theta \sin\phi \cos\phi \big\rangle
$$

The vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(\theta,\phi)$ parametrizes the surface defined in spherical polar coordinates as 
$\rho=\theta \sin{\phi}.$
What is the first component of $\mathbf{f}?$
examples.worked_solution:
If $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x = \rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \qquad
y = \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \qquad 
z = \rho\cos\phi
$$

Now, a point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface has the corresponding position vector given by

$$
\mathbf{f} = \big\langle x, \: y, \: z \big\rangle = \big\langle \rho\cos\theta\sin\phi, \: \rho\sin\theta\sin\phi, \: \rho\cos\phi \big\rangle.
$$

Finally, substituting $\rho=\theta \sin{\phi},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\theta ,ϕ) & =⟨\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩ \\  & =⟨\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ,\,\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ,\,\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the first component of $\mathbf{f}$ is ${\color{black}\theta \cos\theta \sin^2 \phi}.$

feedback.problem:
$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\text{_____},\,r\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta ⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(r,\theta )$ parametrizes the surface defined in cylindrical polar coordinates as 
$z=r\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta .$
What is the second component of $f?$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical coordinates of a point and $(x,y,z)$ are the corresponding Cartesian coordinates of that point, then we have

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

Now, a point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface has the corresponding position vector given by

$$
f=⟨x,\,y,\,z⟩=⟨r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩.
$$

Finally, substituting $z=r\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta ,$ we obtain the parametrization

$$
f(r,\theta )=⟨r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,r\operatorname{cos}⁡4\theta ⟩.
$$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$
